title: quantization-exec-path-specs-int8-fp8-gptq-awq-draft-v2
content:
Purpose:
This draft specifies the execution-path constraints and expected kernel semantics for INT8, FP8, GPTQ, and AWQ quantized models in the serving runtime. Goal is to define: kernel feature surface, scheduling implications, KV-cache interactions, fallback behavior, and suggested validation/eval checklist for rollout.

Scope:
- Inference execution paths for decoder-only and encoder-decoder transformer variants.
- Quantization formats targeted: per-channel symmetric INT8, FP8 (e5m2/e4m3), GPTQ (4/8-bit variants per RPT), and AWQ (per-channel 4-bit with grouped scales).
- Hardware targets: NVIDIA A100/H100 (CUDA), select x86 CPU fast-paths, and Triton-backed custom kernels.
- Excludes training-time quantization flow (handled by model-offline toolchain).

Design principles / assumptions:
- Deterministic functional equivalence within acceptable delta compared to FP16 baseline for serving SLOs.
- Kernels may provide fused ops (qlinear gemm + bias + layernorm fuse) when beneficial; fusion must expose correctness and dynamic shape guarantees to scheduler.
- Runtime must be able to route to a compatible kernel variant given model metadata and active hardware pool.
- KV cache layout must remain consistent across quantization fallbacks; if incompatible, runtime should trigger safe rewarm + validation.

Kernel feature surface (per quant type):
1) INT8 (per-channel symmetric)
   - Required: int8 GEMM with per-channel scale/dequantize semantics, int8 matmul + add_bias, support for packed weight layout (OC major), and reversible quantization metadata (scale, zero_point implicitly 0 for symmetric).
   - Optional: fused attention qkv project + matmul when QKV weights also quantized; optimized KV write/read with int8-packed cache entries.
   - Constraints: accumulation in int32 or fp16 depending on hardware; final activation requantize to fp16 or fp32 for subsequent ops (e.g., layernorm). Kernel must declare accumulator type.

2) FP8 (e4m3 / e5m2 variants)
   - Required: conversion kernels between FP8 and FP16/FP32 with correct rounding modes; GEMM path accepting FP8 weights and FP16 activations where HW supports FP8 compute (e.g., H100).
   - Constraints: non-uniform dynamic range requires per-tensor scale metadata; fallback path to FP16 if hardware lacks FP8 native support.
   - Precision guardrail: runtime must optionally enable dynamic range probing at model load (sample a few batches) to sanity-check overflow frequency; flag model as "fp8-unsafe" if overflow > threshold.

3) GPTQ (4-bit / 8-bit variants from offline GPTQ tool)
   - Required: support for grouped scaling and zero-point per-block; matrix multiply kernels that apply per-block dequantization on-the-fly to avoid fully materializing FP32 weights.
   - Constraints: non-linear quantizers (per-block scale + some residual tables) may require additional scratch memory; kernel must report extra_scratch_bytes requirement to scheduler.
   - Fallback: when scratch memory not available, fallback to a slower dequantize-then-gemm path (materialize FP16 block in temporary buffer), with explicit throttling to avoid OOM.

4) AWQ (4-bit asymmetric weight quantization)
   - Required: asymmetric decode logic (scale + bias per group), compatibility with grouped matrix layouts, and a fast path for attention projection where AWQ grouped blocks align with GPU tensor cores.
   - Constraints: AWQ may change the numerical distribution of KV writes - verify that KV cache quantized storage (if used) preserves retrieval fidelity.

Shared kernel requirements:
- Shape & dynamic batching: kernels must accept variable sequence lengths and batch sizes; where not possible, kernel registration must include supported max_seq and max_batch and a fallback path must exist.
- KV-cache integration: kernels that write KV cache should expose the exact memory layout and quantization semantics to the KV manager so cache reads/writes are zero-copy when possible. If kernel uses packed int8/awq formats in cache, the KV manager must be able to map to that format or trigger re-encoding at write time.
- Metadata: model artifact must include quantization metadata file (qmeta.json) listing per-layer quant scheme, axes, scales, block_size, and suggested kernel tag. Kernel selection is runtime-configurable via tag precedence (explicit mapping > hardware capability > recommended).
- Scratch & temporary memory: kernel registration must expose worst-case scratch bytes per batch and per-seq to the scheduler for allocation planning.

Scheduling implications and policies:
- Admission control must account for per-request extra_scratch_bytes. For GPTQ/AWQ paths, scheduler should prefer batching requests with similar seq_lens to reuse dequantization buffers.
- Preferred placement policy: route FP8 workloads to HW with native FP8 support first; fall back to FP16 emulation only when capacity constrained and at degraded perf.
- Pre-warm & probe: when a model with new quant format is pinned to a node pool, runtime should run a short probe workload (5-20 requests) to validate numerical stability and check for overflows/NaNs. Probe failures degrade to safer path.
- Canarying: rollout of quantized kernels should be canaried per-policy (small percentage traffic) with metrics tracked: token-latency, generation divergence vs FP16 baseline (embedding similarity, BLEU/ROUGE where relevant), error rates.

KV cache specifics:
- Storage format: default KV cache store is fp16 unless model/kernel indicates compatible packed quantized cache. Packed cache (int8/4bit) is allowed only if all participating kernels (read/write) support the same packing semantics.
- Read/write contract: KV write path must include a version tag and quant-format tag; KV read must validate format match. On mismatch, runtime may: 1) transparently re-encode cache on the fly (costly) OR 2) invalidate cache for that session and re-warm. Decision controlled by per-customer policy.
- Partial cache updates: attention caching with quantized weight matrices requires attention to accumulation error; recommend conservative retention window when using 4-bit caches (i.e., prefer shorter session lengths).

Validation & testing checklist:
- Unit kernels: numeric tolerance tests vs FP16 baseline for matmul/bias/gelu/layernorm under varied seqlen/batch. Thresholds: mean relative error < 1e-3 for INT8/GPTQ typical; FP8 tighter depending on format.
- Integration: end-to-end generation tests with representative prompts: check output divergence metrics (embedding cos similarity, token sync) and perf regression.
- Memory pressure: stress tests that push scratch allocations to ensure graceful fallback without OOM.
- KV correctness: replay tests that write cache with quantized kernel and read back across kernel variants; assert bit-level or numeric compatibility depending on format.

Open questions / action items:
- (A1) Define exact error thresholds per quant scheme for alerting (suggestions above, need product sign-off).
- (A2) Decide default KV policy for heterogeneous pools (prefer re-encoding vs invalidate). Engineering preference: re-encode by default for Hosted but invalidate for Private to avoid unpredictable CPU/memory spikes.
- (A3) Add explicit per-layer kernel hint in qmeta.json to support forced kernel mapping during A/B experiments.

Implementation notes / timeline suggestions:
- Phase 0 (2 weeks): Formalize qmeta.json schema and kernel registration API (include scratch_bytes, tags, supported_formats).
- Phase 1 (4-6 weeks): Implement INT8 fast-path kernels + allocator/scheduler hooks; unit tests and small canary.
- Phase 2 (6-8 weeks): FP8 native path integration for H100/A100 variants + probing tooling.
- Phase 3 (6-10 weeks): GPTQ and AWQ kernel work and KV cache packed format support, extended stress testing.

Backward compatibility / fallback rules (runtime behavior):
- If kernel for requested quant format is unavailable: try secondary compatible kernel (e.g., GPTQ -> INT8 emulation -> FP16 dequantize).
- If scratch memory insufficient: queue request with backoff and try smaller batch or degrade to FP16 path.
- Instrumentation: every fallback must emit a telemetry event with reason, latency impact estimate, and model_id.

Notes / references:
- See ENG-1423 (linked) for prior perf numbers and A/B notes.
- Slack thread: #serving-runtime-quant (discussion on FP8 overflow heuristics).
- Related PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/438 (experimental FP8 kernels).

Next steps:
- Review with applied-ml and serving-runtime kernel owners (Tom/Aisha) to finalize numeric thresholds and qmeta schema.
- Create implementation tickets for kernel registration API and KV packed-cache support (assign to Diego).

This is a working draft - expect edits and incremental additions.
